title: The Treasury Collateral Spread and Levered Safe-Asset Production
eligible_reason: No staggered binary design. The only DiD (analysis/code/regression_euro_diff_in_diff.do) is a single-date event: post = date >= 11 Jul 2011 for every CUSIP (European bank stress), treat = top half of European-bank collateral share in Apr 2011 (pooled treated-group dummy, no CUSIP FE), monthly Treasury-CUSIP panel Feb-Nov 2011, with time-varying controls (duration, lagged bid-ask, on-the-run, CTD, special, maturity) in every column, split by collateral-ratio bucket; columns 3 and 6 add month FE. All other main results are time-series regressions (ivreg2 Newey-West) of the collateral spread on repo/leverage measures, or CUSIP-day regressions of yield residuals on the continuous collateral ratio.
design_notes: Stata (reghdfe, ivreg2) plus Python notebooks. Model plus measurement paper on the Treasury collateral spread using confidential FR 2052a repo data. Euro DiD: reg return_monthly_bps post##treat + 7 controls if g_2collat_contemp==2/1, [aw=weight] in cols 2-3/5-6, vce(cluster tcusip_id).
data_files_note: README: confidential supervisory data (FR 2052a repo, interdealer specials) replaced by *_pseudo.dta files 'with the correct structure but with random placeholder data'; CRSP Treasury files, Markit, Bloomberg, JP Morgan and SEC N-MFP must be obtained by the replicator. build/output (compiled_UST_sec_sorted_monthly.dta used by the DiD) is not shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract. Single common event date with a pooled treated dummy and controls; not staggered, not a near-miss.
data_provenance_note: Data needed for the DiD (CRSP Treasury + SEC N-MFP) not shipped; confidential inputs shipped only as random pseudo data (synthetic).
software_notes: Stata 15+ (reghdfe, ivreg2, astile), Python 3.11 notebooks for build steps.
